# Upgrading to 0.3

0.3 makes the agent-first changes of [ADR-018](adrs/018-agent-first-api.md) and the hierarchical states of
[ADR-019](adrs/019-hierarchical-states-and-history-at-scale.md). Each breaking change has a note below with
code before and after. Nothing here needs a manual data migration: the one stored shape that changes (an
actor with states) is rewritten when the Durable Object loads it.

## testActor runs the runtime's step core (ADR-018 D)

`testActor()` now runs every message through the same `step()` core as the Durable Object and
`simulate()`. Three things that used to pass in tests now behave as they do in production.

**Timers must be declared.** Scheduling a timer the actor does not declare (or with a payload its schema
refuses) throws, as it does in the Worker.

```ts
// Before: recorded, though the Worker would refuse it
messages: { PLAN: message(z.object({}), (s, _p, ctx) => { ctx.schedule("tick", { in: "5s" }); return s; }) },

// After: declare it
messages: { PLAN: message(z.object({}), (s, _p, ctx) => { ctx.schedule("tick", { in: "5s" }); return s; }) },
timers: { tick: timer(z.undefined(), (s) => s) },
```

**Actors with states return the persisted state.** `init` and `send` give `{ shared, phase, local,
stateTimers }`, typed per phase (before, `testActor` could not run them).

```ts
// Before: simulate() only
const sim = simulate({ contracts: [QuizContract] });

// After
const t = testActor(QuizContract);
const s0 = t.init({}); // { shared, phase: "lobby", local: null, stateTimers: [] }
const s1 = (await t.send(s0, "ann", { type: "START" })).state;
if (s1.phase === "round") s1.local.n; // typed
```

**Refusals carry a code.** A refused message still rejects with an `Error`; it is now a `RefusalError`
whose `code` says why.

```ts
// Before
await expect(t.send(s, "bob", { type: "END" })).rejects.toThrow("Guard rejected");

// After (the message still works; the code is stable)
const error = await t.send(s, "bob", { type: "END" }).catch((e) => e);
expect(error.code).toBe("guard_failed");
```

## Refusals are typed values with a code, a sentence and a docs link (ADR-018 C)

`simulate().send`, the Durable Object's `send()` RPC (and `ActorRef.send`) return
`{ ok: true } | Refusal`, where a `Refusal` is
`{ ok: false, code, message, expected?, details?, docs }`. The codes are `unknown_message`,
`invalid_payload`, `guard_failed`, `wrong_state`, `no_role`, `not_initialized`, `invalid_delivery` and
`actor_not_found`. Two old codes were renamed: `message_not_found` → `unknown_message`,
`validation_failed` → `invalid_payload`. `detail` is gone: Zod issues are in `details`.

```ts
// Before
expect(room.send("bob", { type: "CLOSE" })).toEqual({ ok: false, error: "guard_failed" });
const r = await stub.send("u", "user", { type: "ADD", n: "x" });
if (!r.ok && r.error === "validation_failed") console.log(r.detail);

// After
expect(room.send("bob", { type: "CLOSE" })).toMatchObject({ ok: false, code: "guard_failed" });
const r = await stub.send("u", "user", { type: "ADD", n: "x" });
if (!r.ok && r.code === "invalid_payload") console.log(r.message, r.details, r.docs);
```

A message refused in the wrong state reads, for example, `ANSWER is accepted in round; the actor is in
lobby.` with `expected: ["round"]` and `details: { phase: "lobby" }`.

## The `__error` frame and the client's `onError` (ADR-018 C)

A refused WebSocket message now gets `{ type: "__error", messageType, code, message, expected?,
details?, docs }`, and `onError` receives a `ClientError` with the same fields (`code` is
`"invalid_frame"` for an error frame the client cannot read).

```ts
// Before
createActorClient({ ..., onError: ({ message, error }) => toast(`${message}: ${error}`) });

// After
createActorClient({ ..., onError: (e) => toast(`${e.messageType}: ${e.message}`) });
```

## Thrown errors carry `code` and `docs` (ADR-018 C)

Every error the library throws is an `ActorKitError` (from `@actor-kit/core`) or a subclass
(`NondeterminismError`, `JournalDivergenceError`, `RefusalError`, ...), with a stable `code` and a `docs`
URL (`https://actorkit.dev/errors/<code>/`). Messages are unchanged or extended with how to fix the
problem, so match on `code` rather than on message text.

```ts
// Before
expect(() => run()).toThrow('Timer "tick" is not declared on this actor');

// After
expect(() => run()).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ code: "undeclared_timer" }));
```

`ActorRef.send` on a binding that is not an actor-kit Durable Object resolves with an `actor_not_found`
refusal (was `{ ok: false, error: "stub.send not available" }`).

## One way to define an actor: `kit.actor` (ADR-018 A)

`setup()` takes `events`, `states` and `env`, all optional, and its kit defines the actor. The kit supplies
`events` and `env`, so the definition no longer repeats them; with `states`, `initial` must name a declared
state and every declared state needs its definition (both checked by the compiler).

```ts
// Before
const quiz = setup({ events, states });
export const Quiz = defineActor("quiz", { events: quiz.events, initial: "lobby", states: { ... }, ... });

// After
const quiz = setup({ events, states });
export const Quiz = quiz.actor("quiz", { initial: "lobby", states: { ... }, ... });
// or: defineActor("quiz", quiz, { ... })
```

An actor with nothing to declare uses `setup({})`:

```ts
// Before
export const Counter = defineActor("counter", { messages: { INC: message(z.object({}), (s: S) => s) }, ... });

// After
const counter = setup({});
export const Counter = counter.actor("counter", { messages: { INC: counter.message(z.object({}), (s: S) => s) }, ... });
```

`defineActor(name, def)` still works for a whole definition, but docs and examples use the kit.

**The standalone `message()` / `timer()` no longer type `ctx.emit` loosely.** Their context's `emit`
accepts no event name (the actor declares none). Emit through the kit's helpers instead.

```ts
// Before (compiled; checked only at runtime)
BID: message(z.object({ amount: z.number() }), (s, p, ctx) => { ctx.emit("BidPlaced", p); return s; }),

// After
const auction = setup({ events: { BidPlaced: z.object({ amount: z.number() }) } });
BID: auction.message(z.object({ amount: z.number() }), (s: S, p, ctx) => { ctx.emit("BidPlaced", p); return s; }),
```

## Service calls: handles, result limits, Evicted (ADR-018 G)

**`onError` can receive `{ _tag: "Evicted" }`.** A try cut off by an eviction now counts as an attempt
(it used to run again without counting). When it was the last attempt, `onError` runs with this new
built-in error, so exhaustive checks over the error union need a branch for it.

```ts
// Before
onError: (s, error) => (error._tag === "Timeout" ? retryLater(s) : giveUp(s, error.message)),

// After
onError: (s, error) =>
  error._tag === "Timeout" || error._tag === "Evicted" ? retryLater(s) : giveUp(s, error._tag === "Defect" ? error.message : error._tag),
```

**A try cut off by an eviction waits for its backoff** (it is `retrying`, not `pending`, on wake).

**Results are limited to 128 KiB of JSON** (`maxResultBytes` per service); a larger result fails the try
as a `Defect`. Return a reference instead, or raise the limit.

```ts
// Before: a 1 MB result was journaled as is
report: { fn: async () => bigReport() },

// After
report: { fn: async () => ({ url: await storeReport(await bigReport()) }) },
// or, if it must be inline: report: { maxResultBytes: 2_000_000, fn: async () => bigReport() },
```

**`ctx.execute()` returns the effect id, and `ctx.cancel(id)` also cancels calls.** Code that typed
`execute` as returning `void` keeps compiling; a timer key you chose that looks like an effect id
(`"12:0"`) would now also cancel the execution with that id, so pick keys that are not `seq:index`.

```ts
// Before
ctx.execute("charge", input);

// After (optional)
const id = ctx.execute("charge", input); // "812:0"
ctx.cancel(id); // later, from another handler
```

`effectInfo()` (from `@actor-kit/worker/testing`, for hand-built service tests) now takes an `audit` object
and returns `record()`.

## Journal format for 0.3 (ADR-018 F)

**Callbacks can emit, and a callback that only emits is journaled.** Lifecycle, service and link
callbacks get `ctx.emit` (typed by the kit's events; use `kit.service()` and `kit.link()` for services
and links). Before, a lifecycle or service callback that changed nothing was not journaled.

```ts
// Before: no emit in callbacks; events had to be emitted by a follow-up message
services: { charge: { fn, onDone: (s, r) => ({ ...s, paid: true }) } },

// After
services: {
  charge: kit.service({ fn, onDone: (s: S, r, _i, ctx) => { ctx.emit("Paid", { id: ctx.effectId }); return { ...s, paid: true }; } }),
},
links: { feed: kit.link(Feed, { onUpdate: (s: S, view, _id, ctx) => { ctx.emit("Synced", view); return s; } }) },
```

**A standalone `link()` types `ctx.emit` like a kit without events** (no event accepted); use
`kit.link()` to emit from link callbacks.

**Rebuilds by replay compare emitted events.** A `rebuild: "replay"` version now fails with
`JournalEmittedDivergenceError` when the new handlers emit different events than were recorded. If you
renamed or reshaped an event on purpose, say so in the step:

```ts
// Before
version(2, StateV2, { rebuild: "replay" }),

// After
version(2, StateV2, {
  rebuild: "replay",
  renames: { BidPlaced: "BidMade" },
  emitted: { BidPlaced: (p) => ({ ...p, currency: "USD" }) },
}),
```

**Refused messages are recorded** (a new `rejections` table, migration `0018_rejections`, created on
wake); nothing to change in your code.

## Determinism in production (ADR-018 E)

Handlers now run under the determinism guard in the Worker too. With the default `determinism: "warn"`
nothing fails: a handler that reads `Date.now()`, `new Date()`, `Math.random()`, `crypto.randomUUID()` and
the like gets the real value, but the runtime logs an `actor_kit.handler.nondeterministic` line and flags
the journal entry (replay cannot reproduce it). Fix the handler, or choose the mode:

```ts
// Before: no option; production never checked
export const Game = defineActor("game", { ... });

// After: the same behaviour plus the warning (default), or fail like the tests do
export const Game = game.actor("game", { determinism: "throw", ... }); // "warn" | "throw" | "off"
```

```ts
// Before (warned in production from 0.3, throws in tests)
PLACE: game.message(z.object({}), (s: S) => ({ ...s, at: Date.now(), id: crypto.randomUUID() })),

// After
PLACE: game.message(z.object({}), (s: S, _p, ctx) => ({ ...s, at: ctx.now(), id: ctx.id() })),
```

To catch these before tests run, enable the Biome plugin:
`"plugins": ["./node_modules/@actor-kit/worker/biome/no-nondeterminism.grit"]`.

## The phase is a path; locals and scoped timers are per level (ADR-019 A)

States nest, so the persisted state of an actor with states is now
`{ shared, phase, locals, stateTimers }`: `phase` is the path from the root (`["round"]` for a flat
actor), `locals` has one local per level and `stateTimers` one list of keys per level. A Durable Object
stored in the 0.2 shape (`{ shared, phase: "round", local, stateTimers }`) is read as its one-element
path when it loads, and written in the new shape on its next transition; `phasedState()` reads both.

`ctx.phase` in handlers, guards, `enter` and `exit` is the path too. Views and roles narrow with
`matches()` (a path prefix, typed) and read the merged local with `localOf()`, since TypeScript cannot
narrow a union on a tuple element.

```ts
// Before
const project = (st: QuizState) => ({
  phase: st.phase,
  round: st.phase === "round" ? st.local.n : 0,
});
expect(q.state).toEqual({ shared, phase: "lobby", local: null, stateTimers: [] });

// After
import { localOf, matches } from "@actor-kit/worker";
const project = (st: QuizState) => ({
  phase: st.phase.join("."),
  round: matches(st, "round") ? localOf(st).n : 0,
});
expect(q.state).toEqual({ shared, phase: ["lobby"], locals: [null], stateTimers: [[]] });
```

Handlers are unchanged: `ctx.local`, `ctx.stay`, `ctx.goto("round", ...)` and `kit.in("round")` work as
before (a name is the one-element path). Refusals still name states as text (`playing.window`).
`enter` may now return `ctx.stay(shared, local)` to change the shared state, and a state may declare
`exit(shared, ctx)`, `initial` and child `states`.
